items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the round-feedback form after the sprint-47 live clicks); filed by Claude
items.title: Roads are a tree plus a detour test, and only villages above a size spur: no lattice, and round 6's tail inside 35 s
items.design:
MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 50. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-25, the density form): the village spur floor is 40,000 heads (the ladder's ~p90; median road pass 18 s loaded, 1 of 16 seeds under 10 s), size read as the population step's headcount; a border link ends ONLY on a town or a spurring village (LOGISTICS.md § 4). The street carpet is not this item's: BL-1130 (centres consolidate) thins the centres upstream, and this item's "no lattice on the densest seed" is read after it.

ROUND 2 (the lane's own findings and the settle review): fix the floor at 40,000 as the constant; border endpoints restricted to towns and spurring villages; road_generation.cpp's two hand-written cache clears (~616-619, ~689-691) replaced by invalidate_logistics_caches so the new nearest-anchor field is never missed; the loading bar's roads weight (hard_coded_world.cpp ~495, 38,000 ms) and kBorderUnitsPerNation re-measured; road_generation_harness's "R2 highway tier reachable when qualified" FAILS on 0 of 8 seeds, identically on b03fd52e -- find why (the percentile gate, the two-major-endpoints rule, or the harness's qualified regen) and fix the cause or split it to its own item with the reading; never weaken the row.

SPRINT 48 CUT (Ben, 2026-09-25, the cut form): BL-1077 (village roads cost) is FOLDED IN. Its target joins this done-when: generate_roads under ~10 s Release on the library seeds, read after the spur floor; if the floor alone does not reach it, BL-1077's bound (one multi-source search per centre, or a shared reach field, digest-neutral by itself) is this item's second step. THE 35 s IS JUDGED ON THE WHOLE TAIL, jointly with BL-1117 (settle tick one), which joins the sprint with its fix: on seed 0 the settle is ~56 s Release, tick 1 alone 38.5 s, so roads alone cannot meet it.

FILED 2026-09-25 (Ben, walking round 6: "we also need many fewer roads... it should be heavily discouraged to build a lattice of roads"; he chose the tree plus a detour test over "no second path", and spurs only for villages above a size). LOGISTICS.md § 4 carries the rule; STARTUP.md § Round 6 carries the 35 s target.

THE WORK. (1) Replace the relative-neighbour redundancy edges with the DETOUR TEST: after the Kruskal MST, a candidate link between two centres is laid only when the network's route between them costs more than 2x the direct A* route (one constant, named). The percentile rationing of loops applies to the loops the test admits (a delegated reading that keeps BL-618/BL-621 intact; Ben may overturn). (2) A village lays a spur only above a size floor, MEASURED on the 16 curated seeds first (Rule 0b: road tiles, spur count and pass time per floor candidate). (3) The border link rule is unchanged.

A WORLD-MOVER: every road digest and the sweep pins move -- read road tile counts, pass time (gen_step_costs --finish) and the haulage baseline (memory: goldens cannot see trade) on the 16 seeds before and after, then ONE re-bless.

DONE WHEN. No lattice on a capture of the densest seed; road pass time and tile count recorded old -> new per seed; round 6's tail lands within 35 s of arrival on seeds 0 and 28 in Release (gen_step_costs); one re-bless; road_generation_harness green (connectivity held). CARRIED to sprint 49 at the sprint 48 close (2026-10-04): owed R4 a quiet Release gen_step_costs run on 16 seeds (road tiles and pass time per seed, old -> new, against ~10 s); R6 an isolated haulage reading of this change (or fold into BL-1165); R7 a cold review of round 4 (8b921ee6, directed paths).

items.title: A built processor gets its inputs: 85% running and at most 5% input-starved at handoff
items.design: TARGETS RAISED (Ben, 2026-10-08): G1 >= 85% running at handoff, plus G1b <= 5% input-starved (now, or decommissioned after starving), 16 seeds. 70% had no recorded reason beyond a first stretch from a 17.6% baseline; G1 alone counts a plant idled for want of a buyer as failure, so starvation gets its own target. CARRIED from sprint 49 (Ben, the close-out form, 2026-10-07: close with G1 unmet, carry it to sprint 50 as a logistics item). The 16-seed market_viability reading on main after BL-1183 C1: G1 54.7% of built processors running at handoff against Ben's 70% (G2 54.4 and G3 88.9 pass). About a quarter of built processors are already decommissioned by the handoff, and by their last reported state almost all were input-starved (half A: 578 of 674). Diagnose which inputs fail to arrive, at which markets, and why - no producer within reach, a producer whose surplus is not dispatched, or a dispatch the margin refuses - then fix the cause in the network or dispatch, not by clamping the loss reflex. Re-measure construction stalls here too: whether a stalled site is ever abandoned (BL-1183 C3) is still unruled. Judge it on the market-viability skill, 16 seeds.

items.author: Claude (sprint 50, deferred by Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: Long-term viability: plants running at handoff are still running at play tick 50
items.design: DEFERRED from sprint 50 (Ben, 2026-10-09: 'push the long term viability work for another sprint, after the various other gameplay loops are settled'). Target carried: G1 at tick 50 >= 85% (market-viability; reported, not gated, in sprint 50). FOUND (starve_trace_probe, f98d43df, shipped code before sprint 50's wave 2b): of 665 plants lost handoff->t50, 386 starved. (1) STEEL: a background-firm CONSTRUCTION BOOM - on 33 starving markets 725 sites draw steel at t50, 701 background-owned (ports/hubs 264, food 181, fuel 79); site need ~373/tick vs processors ~35; making builds read steel scarcity is a NEW AI GRANT (raise it). (2) UNDELIVERED HAULS: copper ore - dispatcher 'would send' in 36/47 cases, arrivals ~8/tick; split Logistic Points cap / one-destination-per-pass / goods sent elsewhere (SUPPLY/LOGISTICS). (3) POOL-HELD STOCK: 42 plants starve while stock sits unlisted in other pools at the market; split processor reservation vs sell-order floor (MARKETS). (4) FUEL->PROPELLANT COLD START: with generation bounded by want, neither chain stands at generation and no launchpad exists on any seed; space access depends on settle/play building both (PRODUCTION, ERAS gate). Ruled healthy, keep: fair-price ceiling (cf off: -8.0 G1t50), background pull (cf off: -1.4), households' first draw. Re-measure with the probe after sprint 50 merges before designing.

items.author: Claude (sprint 50 PROPELLANT cold review; backlogged by Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: A rival's launch fuel is not drained by its own scorer or the space programme - or it is, by ruling
items.design: BACKLOGGED by Ben (2026-10-09, launch fuel form) - both questions open, for a ruling when space access matters. Context: MARKETS.md step 4 reserves a pad pool's propellant from auto-surplus (Ben 2026-10-09; may still be sold by a standing order). Cold review of the PROPELLANT lane found three rival paths that ignore that reservation: (a) corp_ai.cpp listable_surplus (~2572) uses processor_reservation, so the trade candidate places an uncapped sell order that empties the pad pool, re-placed each time stock rebuilds; (b) the scorer's directed dispatch (~2735) has no reservation and can haul pad propellant to the capital market on the same body; (c) space_programme.cpp (~140-175) buys 50-unit lumps from the pool holding most unreserved stock - pad pools are now where propellant piles up. Q1: should the scorer sell/haul only above the pad reservation? Q2: should the space programme buy only the excess? No seed had a launchpad at t50 in sprint 50, so the effect is latent.

items.author: Claude (from the BL-1287 seed-13 diagnosis)
items.title: Do ruined roads recover? A corridor the fall decayed below its traffic rung is never rebuilt unless traffic walks it
items.design: OPEN (design question for Ben). BL-1287's fall decays the falling realm's roads on the ground (Ben, 2026-10-12). Measured 2026-10-13 (tools/verify/rise_fall_roads.cpp): about 6 corridors per seed stay below the rung their own traffic earned from 1200 to 1960, because nothing rebuilds a corridor traffic does not walk and the resumed spans reopen it at the decayed tier. Works relief over-recovers (waystations buy it back). Small effect; not a cause of G1b. Options: ruins recover toward their earned rung over the following span; or ruins persist as a visible scar. items.author: Ben (2026-10-16 playtest); filed by Claude
items.title: The Life round's Reroll gives the same landmasses: it moves ocean/oxygen only, never the plates
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16 playtest): "reroll in life doesn't reroll the seed. I'm still getting similar landmasses either way." CONFIRMED: the press increments preferences.roll[1] (startup_screens.cpp:2866), which perturbs only resolve_preferences' rb stream - home_ocean, oxygenation, coal_climate (planetology.cpp:385). run_continents is seeded from params.seed ^ prototype_body_seed(1) (hard_coded_world.cpp:596) and reads only mobile_lid and theta, both from roll[0]. So plates, drift and the height-bias field are bit-identical across any number of Life rerolls; only sea level moves. Fold the round's roll into the body seed handed to run_continents (or move params.seed) so a Reroll re-draws the landmasses.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16 playtest); filed by Claude
items.title: A road is an edge between two tiles, not a property of one
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16 playtest): 'Roads should be directional, so they always cross the edge of two tiles.' RULED (Ben, 2026-10-16): roads move to EDGES, as rivers already are - not a rendering-only change. DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section 4 (Roads - an edge between two tiles) and RENDERING.md (Roads draw across the edge they cross). Grain: a tier per hex side, six sides, two bits each (0 none / 1 Track / 2 Road / 3 Highway), both tiles of an edge carrying it as both tiles of a river crossing do, side i mirroring side i+3. The road multiplier moves from the node to the EDGE in logistics.cpp edge_cost, beside the river discount that already lives there (A* keeps its 4-cardinal walk and its hex_side_for_offset derivation). Every count of roaded TILES becomes a count of roaded EDGES, each edge once: Logistic Points, network upkeep, reach, interdiction. Placement names a tile AND a side. Pre-v53 saves migrate by laying, between each pair of 4-cardinal neighbours that both carried a road, an edge at the LOWER of their two tiers. World save v53 claimed. A WORLD-MOVER: measure haulage_measure --far-trade and market_viability before and after; a re-bless is Ben's.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16 playtest); filed by Claude
items.title: The build card never says a second of the same type may stand on the tile, or how to add it
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16 playtest): 'We should be able to build multiple of the same building on one tile' then, clarifying: 'it's not clear how to build the second level.' So nothing refused him - the rule already permits stacking (non_extraction_stack_cap 2-12 in AGGREGATE across every non-extraction type, placement_rules.cpp:557; extraction max(1, richness/50) per deposit). It is an AFFORDANCE defect in the construction ledger's build list: the row shows a type once and never says Build adds to the stack, nor how much room the tile has left. The card should carry how many stand and how much room remains, in wording that does not imply the non-extraction room is per type, and must not read like the road/rail ladder rows beside it, which are upgrades-in-place. A full tile's refusal should name what filled it (aggregate cap, per-deposit cap, or the province ceiling at placement_rules.cpp:479). No cap or rule changes.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16 playtest); filed by Claude
items.title: Construction shows ETA 2 qtr and never moves: the UI's rate mirror reads different numbers from the sim
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16 playtest): "construction stall when there appears to be enough goods. ETA 2 qtr, but no progress for multiple quarters." CONFIRMED divergence: ui::construction_rate (construction_panel.cpp:35) reads m->supply[r] (the per-tick FLOW, reset every tick) where run_construction draws m->inventory[r] (persistent stock); it omits capacity_per_build_tick from the need row (so a capacity-starved site reads on-schedule while the sim stretches it up to 10x); it ignores the shelf_admits fair-price ceiling (a good above reservation_mult x base is zero to the sim); and it ignores plan_short_shelves rationing and state_idle. construction.md:71 asserts the mirror matches run_construction - that claim is false. Make the UI read what the sim reads, and name the blocking good on the status line so a stall says why.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16 playtest); filed by Claude
items.title: The construction queue says "No active construction" while buildings are building, and no construction shows a progress bar
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16 playtest): "the construction queue is showing 'No active construction', when there are multiple buildings being constructed" and "We should show a progress bar on constructions." The placeholder is hard-coded: const bool any_items = false (construction_panel.cpp:160) with the 5-column table dead behind it, while the same file's estimated_quarterly_construction_cost already walks w.buildings for ticks_remaining > 0. There is no construction_queue container and none is needed. Progress is computable at every draw site from ticks_remaining, construction_progress and construction_build_ticks (or construction_paid / construction_capex, which cannot drift when roads or the stack change).

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16 playtest); filed by Claude
items.title: The build card should show the cost in resources and credits and what the building produces, and drop payback
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16 playtest): "change building tiles in construction to show the cost of building it in both resources and credits, and then the output resource or effect, rather than just the credits expected. And we should remove the 'payback' portion." Card: draw_construction_ledger_body (selection_panel.cpp:3758-3875); payback is inline at :3807 as capex / profit.net() and is pessimistic ~2x because the estimate assumes 50% staffing. Everything needed is already in scope: reg.resource_build_cost_for(type, target, recipe) for materials, reg.get_recipe(c.recipe)->inputs/outputs for the output, c.target for extraction. Drop the payback clause and the caption that points at it.

items.author: Claude (found building BL-1339, 2026-10-16)
items.title: A later round's reroll can move an earlier round's committed draws, through the viability attempt index
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found verifying BL-1339, 2026-10-16). planetology.cpp's comment on the three preference streams claims 'bumping a later round's reroll counter cannot disturb an earlier round's already-committed draw'. That is FALSE: resolve_preferences folds the rejection attempt index k into all three streams (ra/rb/rc), so a Life roll that changes how many attempts the world needs moves the SYSTEM draws too. Observed by tools/verify/life_reroll.cpp: campaign seed 0 roll 7 resolves at attempt 2 and theta moves 1.519 -> 1.462, plate count 9 -> 8; seed 7 roll 3 resolves at attempt 3. Pre-dates BL-1339 (it was already true of the three Life draws) and is only now measured. THE CALL IS BEN'S: either the System draws become attempt-independent (so an accepted round really is committed), or the doc and the comment stop claiming independence. A doc and the code disagree, so one of them is wrong and the fix is work.
